title: Jellyfish blooms restructure plankton dynamics and trophic linkages in coastal waters
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Jellyfish blooms are increasing globally in frequency and intensity, introducing complex ecological interactions, yet the mechanisms by which they alter ecosystem structure remain poorly characterized due to a lack of sustained field observations. We conducted targeted time-series observations in Jiaozhou Bay, a representative coastal ecosystem experiencing an Aurelia coerulea bloom, tracking temporal responses of plankton communities and trophic interactions to fluctuations in the jellyfish population. Combining empirical modelling with field data, we further quantified the dual roles of jellyfish as top-down predators and bottom-up nutrient regenerators, linking bloom dynamics to changes in plankton structure and biogeochemical cycling. During high A. coerulea aggregation, the structure of the plankton changed markedly, characterized by a sharp decline in zooplankton coupled with the proliferation of phytoplankton. The top-down feeding effect triggered potential cascading impacts, decoupling trophic pathways by weakening zooplankton-mediated energy transfer and releasing phytoplankton from grazing pressure. Concurrently, jellyfish contributed to biogeochemical processes by releasing bioavailable ammonium and phosphate (low N/P ratio < 16), with phosphate regeneration playing a particularly critical role in stimulating primary production. Overall, this study demonstrates that jellyfish blooms act as ecological disturbances, restructuring plankton dynamics and trophic linkages and ultimately destabilizing local ecosystem functioning. Given the broad distribution and increasing prevalence of jellyfish populations, the findings underscore the need to incorporate jellyfish dynamics into coastal ecosystem-based management, especially for predicting and indicating planktonic regime shifts.

摘要

全球范围内，水母暴发的频率和强度正在增加，引发了复杂的生态相互作用。然而，由于缺乏持续的野外观测，水母暴发改变生态系统结构的机制仍不明确。 我们在胶州湾进行了针对性的时间序列观测，追踪了浮游生物群落和营养相互作用对海月水母种群波动的时间响应。结合经验模型与野外数据，我们进一步量化了海月水母作为自上而下捕食者和自下而上营养再生者的双重作用，将水母爆发动态与浮游生物结构和生物地球化学循环的变化联系起来。 结果发现:在海月水母大量聚集期间，浮游生物结构发生显著变化，表现为浮游动物急剧减少，同时浮游植物大量增殖。自上而下的捕食效应引发了潜在的级联影响，通过削弱浮游动物介导的能量转移并释放浮游植物的被摄食压力，解耦了营养途径。同时，水母通过释放生物可利用的铵盐和磷酸盐(低N/P比，⟨16)促进了生物地球化学过程，其中磷酸盐的再生在刺激初级生产力方面发挥了尤为关键的作用。 总体而言，本研究表明，水母爆发作为一种生态扰动，重构了浮游生物动态和营养联系，并最终破坏了局部生态系统的稳定性。鉴于水母种群的广泛分布和日益增加的普遍性，研究结果强调，需要将水母动态纳入基于沿海生态系统的管理中，特别是在预测和指示浮游生物区系转变方面。
